utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Mr. Chester Stamp, Ms. Tecla Benjamin, Ms. Kimberly Fleming, and Mr. Ekkehard Withopf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence, which has not changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. My name is Edina Residovic. I represent General Hadzihasanovic. Stephane Bourgon is the co-counsel and Ms. Mirna Milanovic is our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Mr. Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, our legal assistant, represent Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom. Before we start hearing the witness, I would like to go into closed session. Mr. Registrar, could we please go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day. I would like to ask you whether you can hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've been called here as a witness for the Prosecution. Could you please give me your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zdravko Pranjes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 12th of July, 1962.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a driver, but I am involved in cattle raising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in 1983, what was your profession? That's ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, I was in Switzerland. I returned in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Where do you live right now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Daruvar, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You will now read out the solemn declaration. Could you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, which is to your right, will put a series of questions to you now. When they have finished with their questions, Defence counsel, which is to your left, will cross-examine you. The Prosecution then might ask you other questions. And the Judges, who are before you, may at any time, if they feel it is necessary, in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Judges will then ask you questions too. Have you understood how the procedure will unfold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So the Prosecution may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pranjes, what municipality and village do you originally hail from?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The village of Maljine in Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is where you were born and raised?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the ethnic breakdown of the population of Maljine?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Half of the population was Muslim and half Croats, but there were more Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that -- I didn't understand an answer you gave about where you were in 1983. I think that was the question. Did you do national service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, in Gospic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you complete that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I went in 1981, and I returned in 1982.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You completed it in 1982?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: After that, I guarded sheep. Then I bought a truck, and I worked with the truck. And I then went to Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period did you live and work in Switzerland? Between what years?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I went in the spring of 1990, and I returned in 1992. I was there for three seasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in about October 1992, did you join the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Frankopan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the Frankopan Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The Frankopan Brigade, Guca Gora -- Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village of Maljine that you're from, that is a village in the district, in the general district of Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. It's 2 and a half kilometres from Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you joined the Frankopan Brigade, where was this unit deployed, in respect to your military duties?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I was in the village, above the village. That's where we went on patrol temporarily. And then above the village there was a place called Zahumlje. It was deployed up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall when you were deployed at Zahumlje?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: That was that autumn. We'd been deployed up there. We'd go up for a week, and then we'd spend a week at 2/6:45 home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still deployed there in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: We were up in Kosarici, a little further on, about 3 or 4 kilometres. We went a little further up. It was another site. That's where we were for Christmas and New Year, at that other site, a little further up towards the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to take you now to early spring of 1993. Where were you deployed then?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: At the beginning of spring, we were still --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, I'd like to intervene to read a Rule from the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with regard to testimony. You have just taken an oath to tell all the truth. The proceedings allow a witness to refuse to make a statement that might incriminate the witness. So if there is a question that you may dislike, you can refuse to answer the question. But the Trial Chamber can oblige you in such a case to respond to such a question. But in such a case, if you do respond to that question, following an order from the Trial Chamber, the testimony that you give can't be used at a subsequent date against you. Have you understood what I said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it is my duty to remind you that a witness has rights, and given the questions put to you, this is a situation that might arise. I would like to ask the Prosecution to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain at your defensive lines at the place you had mentioned up until the spring of 1993, or did you relocate?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: We didn't stay there until spring. We relocated. I don't know exactly when. I couldn't tell you the date. But there were some incidents with the Muslims, and we then withdrew from that place to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which village?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Between Bikose and Maljine. We formed some lines there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "lines," I take it you mean lines of defence to protect the village in case of attack? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, yes, defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the morning of the 4th -- sorry, of the 8th of June, 1993, were you so engaged on these lines of defence?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, I was up there at Greda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is this from where you lived in Maljine?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: It's about 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that morning, at about 4.00 or 5.00, did the Bosnian Muslim army attack your positions?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, at 5.00. That's when they attacked our position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your lines hold, or were they broken?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They were broken, and some went to Guca Gora and others to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "some went to Guca Gora and others to the village," by that, can I take it that you mean some of the defenders, including yourself, retreated to Guca Gora and to the village of Maljine?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Those of us who were nearer to the village, they went to the village; and those who were up there, further up, they could flee through the woods, down towards Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I descended to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to anywhere in particular in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, I reached a stream, and then I went along the stream as far as my house, and then observed a bit, and then I went up to where the hospital was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which hospital was this? Could you briefly describe it for us.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: It was a house, and there were wounded people in the cellar, and my father and some other people were there. My wife was there too. They had taken shelter there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said it was a house. Who operated a hospital at this house?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Ljubica Jakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you retreat to this hospital alone, or were you with anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Jako Tadic was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us where exactly you retreated to. Did you retreat to the hospital itself or to anywhere in the vicinity of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, just before the entrance to the hospital, it's a sort of cellar, and then there are two doors by the hospital, next to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian Muslim army advance to where you had retreated to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. They got up there. There was shooting down in the village. They shot at those they would see. They would shoot at the roofs and all around. There was shooting. I couldn't exactly see what they hit. They'd raised a flag, some kind of a red flag, and there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslim soldiers or the persons in the area where the Muslim soldiers were call out to you and the other retreating personnel, HVO personnel?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They called out to us and asked us to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that done? And if so, how was that arranged?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Ljubica Jakovic and Kata Blazevic went to negotiate with them behind the hospital. And when they returned, they said we had to hand over our weapons and that they should take the weapons over there. That's what happened. We gave them our weapons. They took the weapons there. And later they descended to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they descended to the village, where were you and the other HVO personnel gathered?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: That hospital was at the top of the village, and we set off from there towards the centre, and from the centre we set off in the direction of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But before you set off towards Mehurici, where were you gathered when the Bosnian Muslim army descended into the village, after you had surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Part of us were at the centre, by the road, and the rest of us were still up there, because we didn't know what was going on in the centre. And when the BH army soldiers went down where we were, we collected -- we rallied there and we brought out a woman who was wounded from one of the houses. We took her to the hospital there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: And afterwards, they went round collecting the cars. And there was some questioning going on. And then we moved down towards the centre; that is to say, the group that was at the centre. We left the centre and went out onto the hillside, beside a village, waiting for somebody to find a child that was lost. And then we moved on towards Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Before you leave to Mehurici, let's go back to the point that you were at when the Bosnian Muslim army descended into the village. When you were taken into custody by the Bosnian Muslim army, did you observe who was in charge of the unit that you surrendered to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: There was a blond, young man. I think he was the person in charge. Everybody listened to him. So I assumed that he was the main person there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. There's quite obviously some difference in the Bosnian translation than the transcript, because the translation we received was that the witness was taken into custody, whereas the witness never spoke about custody of any kind. However, the translation into Bosnian was different. So my criticism has no -- my objection has no purpose, because the witness and I heard something different, something that the Prosecutor actually didn't ask him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I thought that I -- I did use the word "custody," but I thought that if he surrendered to someone, he would be in the custody of the persons to whom he surrendered. But never mind. I think I could rephrase it and we could move on from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I wish to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Concerning interpretation problems, I should like to indicate that the difficulty is that we have a witness who is expressing himself in B/C/S and then you have a translation into English and one into French. And sometimes, like you, when I look at the transcript, the transcript has some additional words to it which I did not hear spoken in the French language, in the French interpretation. Let me give you an example. At one particular point, he was saying that in front of the hospital there was a flag, and I saw in English the word "red flag," a red flag; whereas, the French translation, interpretation, didn't have any mention of a red flag. So I don't know what he actually said in the B/C/S language. Did he say "red flag," in B/C/S, which was translated into the English with "red flag"? But anyway, in my French interpretation all I heard was the word "flag" and not "red flag" so sometimes there is lack of precision. So if you notice these, please let us know as you did a moment ago, so we can correct that and avoid going up the wrong road. Because, of course, interpretation is sometimes be a problem. Of course, mostly there are no difficulties, but difficulties may arise. So if you see any problems, please let us know. And of course, there are problems between the B/C/S, English, and French. So if you notice any differences, please let us know. Thank you for your observations. I'd like to give the floor to the Prosecution again now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that a person appeared to be in charge of those to whom you surrendered, because they seemed to be listening to him and obeying him. Did this person appear to be in charge of the Bosnian army unit? Well, how was he dressed? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: He was wearing a green camouflage uniform, and he had a green band round his left arm, and he was wounded. He had a white band round his head, and you could see that the bandage or band was bloody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were his subordinates attired?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms too, and all of them had bands. I didn't notice any separate insignia in the man who was in command or the soldiers. Generally speaking, they were dressed in uniforms, camouflage uniforms with these green bands on their left upper arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described them as members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this -- well, on what basis do you describe them as such? Why do you say they were members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I saw this on television, and they were coming from a Muslim village, so they couldn't be anybody else. It must have been them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just explain. What do you mean you saw this on television? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I saw their army. I had seen them before that. There were lines up there. There was a truce going on. So we played football. So we weren't far away from each other, and I could see them on a daily basis. And afterwards, when the attack took place, they would say "Allah-U-Ekber." That's the term they'd use. And they came from the direction of Mehurici and Suhi Dol, and Donje Maljine too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that they proceeded to take motor vehicles from the village. Could you describe to us what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, there was a car there, a Lada make. It was in my garage but belonged to another man. And they told me to drive the car out of the garage, and then they took it over and drove it off themselves. And they took a cousin's truck away too in the same way. It was an orange Mercedes. Then I saw a white Golf, which was driven off towards Mehurici too, by a Mujahedin. He had a sort of ginger beard and was tall, and he got stuck in the mud and we had to pull him out, as we had -- as we were passing by that way on our way to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took your car -- or who took the car that was parked in your garage? I'm not talking about the name or individual identity of the person who took it, but can you say which army that person was a part of, that is, the person who took the car that was parked in your garage?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The person was a member of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the truck?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The truck was driven off later, not then, not while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having surrendered to these members of the BH army, did they take you and the other HVO personnel anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. They're the ones who took us away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To where?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They took us to -- towards Mehurici. Yes, Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said earlier - and correct me if I'm wrong - that they took you from the place where you surrendered to the centre of the village, where there were other people gathered?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the centre of the village. It's not a big village. And then we went off in the direction of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people were gathered at the centre of the village Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. when you went there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps 200. They were already at the exit to the village, leaving the village. Now, how many people exactly, I can't say. Perhaps 200. They were on the road. They were already on their way to Mehurici. Some of them had -- were already up on the hill. But there were 2 to 3 hundred of us. I don't know exactly. That would be the rough number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 2 do 3 hundred of us. Were these Croatian persons, Croatian prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there only HVO, or were there civilians amongst this crowd of 2 to 3 hundred?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, yes, civilians -- well, when I say "civilians," I mean women, children, young girls. And then there were us, the army. And a lot of them were in civilian clothes, a lot of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you all were forced to set off in the direction of Mehurici. How did you travel?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we travelled in a line of four or five all behind each other on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you escorted on armed soldiers when you travelled to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us which army or which unit the soldiers that escorted you to Mehurici were from.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They were soldiers of the BH army, the ones who had captured us. They were the ones who escorted us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were travelling to Mehurici, did anyone or any group join your group that was travelling there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: From Donje Maljine, there was a man from there who came up to us, and there were some Muslims from Mehurici and Suhi Dol who had come out. There were some children, aged about 15. They were carrying some -- something and then they went back down. We came to the village of Poljanice, and a woman came out and gave us some water to drink, and the children had some of these old-fashioned guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the column or the group of people going towards Mehurici remain as one group, or were you separated?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Most of them stayed intact. That is to say, there was one group until the Mujahedin stopped us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that at that point you were separated.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: We waited for each other, for the groups above the village. And then we moved off together, in one column and didn't separate after that, when we joined up. And when we were 1 to 2 hundred metres away from the Mujahedin houses, where they had their positions, two men came up to us and took away one civilian. Actually, he was a soldier. He was wearing a military uniform. They separated him from the group, and then the army took him off. And then the Mujahedin came up in front of us, taking us by surprise. They were wearing masks and caps on their heads. They stopped us all. And then they separated us one by one there, military-able men. When they had separated the military-able men from amongst our group, that's what happened. We were all together until they separated the military-able men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We have to examine this in a little bit more detail. Can you say where you were at the point when the Mujahedin appeared and separated you -- separated the military-aged men from the body of the group.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I was in the middle, the middle column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your column located at? What part of a road? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I said that it was above the house where the Mujahedin were, their camp. So we had to pass by that house of theirs. And several hundred metres before we came to the house, the Mujahedin stopped us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when they stopped you, were you still being escorted by the BH soldiers that you had surrendered to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, that's where they were, and that's where the BH soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Mujahedin participated in this separation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: When they crossed over the fence onto the road where we were, I saw four or five Mujahedin, and there were just as many who were wearing camouflage uniforms. They cocked their rifles, stood there preparing themselves, and then the soldiers backed off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were these Mujahedin dressed?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, they had some sort of green uniforms, and they had beards, dark beards, big beards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to describe exactly and precisely what happened at the point when they appeared. You said they came over a fence where the column was walking. What happened when they came over the fence?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: When they crossed the hedge, in actual fact, you could hear rifle shots, and they told them to back off. They told the BH soldiers to back off and that they would take the military-able men. They let the women and children go, but they took us military-able men back. And then more of them came up, wearing camouflage uniforms and masked. I don't know how many exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the persons who were not taken by the Mujahedin, did they continue in the direction of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: In the direction of Mehurici, yes. And when they separated us, the civilians - that is to say, the women and children and elderly - went on, but we were stopped. And we had to about-turn, to go back. They told us to go back, whereas the women, children, and elderly were able to continue on their way towards Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many persons were separated from the main group? Just an estimate.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, between 30 and 40 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there -- were there only men who were separated, or were there any women --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: There was one young girl too. She was wearing a camouflage jacket, and she had a sort of red cross or red band on her arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know her name?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Ana Pranjes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall any of the names of any other persons that were taken by the main group by the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: There was Stipan Volic; Ivo Volic, his father; Jako Tavic, Marijanovic Bero, Puselja Zeljo, and Slavko Kramar; Mijo Tavic; Stipo Tavic. There were some other people from some other villages, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you describe to us what happened after you were separated. Were you taken anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: We were taken through the village of Poljanice. And there were some wounded people there from my village at a bend in the road. And Stipo Tavic was also wounded, and he had some rods in his legs. He had been wounded several months previously. So they separated him, and we had to carry him for almost the whole way. When we went round the bend, we saw -- we heard shooting, and I assumed that they had killed them. But we had to carry along our journey, along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons -- the wounded persons you saw from your village, had you seen them before on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They were in the hospital. They were in the hospital that day -- or, rather, that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw them later on on the road, as you just described, were they being guarded by any soldiers or any persons?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. There were two or three soldiers there next to them, and the wounded persons were either lying down or sitting down beside them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These two or three soldiers, which army were they from?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: But I think it was their army that captured them, although I'm not claiming anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "their army," you mean the Bosnian Muslim army, I take it.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, during the examination by my distinguished colleague of the Prosecution, there were leading questions on several occasions; that is, he suggested answers to certain questions. Now, this was all right when it didn't have to do with any important questions but in lines -- and this was in line 10, 12, 17, et cetera. But we didn't want to interrupt the examination-in-chief when a leading question was asked because the witness was very calm in answering all the questions. However, we should like to object now because the witness, asked by the Prosecutor, said that probably there were those with them who took them off, that they were soldiers he didn't know about, didn't know where they came from. And then the question that was the leading question by the Prosecution followed. And we don't consider that that is in order, so may that question and answer be redacted from the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just say that firstly -- I'm not sure about this procedure, in respect to redactions for purposes of this nature. If the question is asked and a matter is in evidence on the record, it's really a matter for the discretion of the Court later on in assessing the probative value of what is being said. I would think the redaction issue would only arise when there are danger issues on needs to protect the witnesses. And we're really speaking here about two armies: The Bosnian Muslim army and the HVO. The witness said there were two or three soldiers. He couldn't say which army. Then in his next answer, he said, "I think it was their army that captured them; although, I'm not claiming anything." So in the context of what he has said so far, when he speaks of "their army," logically and obviously he must be speaking of the Bosnian Muslim army. So the question I asked was merely by way of clarification. I have led the witness in situations like that, and I've done so, it is my submission, within the Rules, in areas where there could not conceivably be any real issue. But nonetheless, I will try not to give my friend any reason to rise. May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is true that line 25 -- in line 25 the Prosecution asked the witness whether those soldiers were members of the BiH army, and the witness said yes. It is true that the witness -- that the question was on the limit. So I think the question could have been formulated differently. Perhaps what should have been asked was could he be more specific on whom the soldiers belonged to, in terms of an armed group. And then he might have said "the BH army" or some other army. So it is true that in line 25 we do have a question which is on the limits. And the Defence was right to rise in objection. However, we're not going to belabour the point. If you would like me to, I could ask the Prosecution to phrase their question in a different way, if they want the witness to give a more specific answer, if he is able to do, and say to the best of his knowledge, for example, or in his opinion, could he say anything more precise. And that may avoid this leading question. So Witness, let me ask you. You said at one point that there were some soldiers who came up close to you. Could you tell us today what unit the soldiers belonged to? If you can tell us. If you don't know, then say so. Because you said that there were some soldiers but you didn't know who they belonged to. So can you identify them or not? Do you understand the sense of my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what is your answer to my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the BH army captured all of us and we were under their control there, but each soldier was not in uniform. One of them had a jacket; another one didn't have anything; the third soldier had, let's say, a jacket and trousers. So I passed by, but I wasn't really in a position to look. But I assume that that was the BH army guarding them there, because the Mujahedin appeared. If there had been any other troops, naturally I wouldn't have waited there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is an assumption of yours. You can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know any of them, so I can't be certain of this. They took a wounded man, took him with us up there and shot him. I don't think this was the Army of Republika Srpska or the Army of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But as you can see, it's necessary to exercise caution when formulating your questions, in that it is for the witness to testify as to what he saw in response to your questions. And to the extent that it is possible, he should avoid any inferences or assumptions. The witness has to testify about facts that he is certain of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. As it pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that as you turned a bend after you'd seen these wounded people you heard gunfire and you made an assumption as to their fate. Have you seen any of these persons alive since then, or do you know if anybody has seen them alive since then?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were aware of a general appearance of the members of the BH army because of your previous association with them. And you also said, in answer to Mr. President, that the BH army captured all of us and you were under the control of the BH army. When you were separated from the main group -- that is, the group of soldiers -- did the BH army personnel there do anything?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: No, they didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you turned the bend and you heard the gunshots behind you, did you and your group proceed to anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. We proceeded towards Bikose by road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who, if anyone, escorted you along the road to Bikose?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The Mujahedin were by us and they had masks, black caps, and they were carrying rifles, and they told us the direction we should take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of them have masks?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: No. About half of them had masks, and the other half didn't. And that's as far as the Mujahedin are concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Bikose, did they take you anywhere or did they have you marched anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: When we arrived in Bikose, the first one who arrived reached a wall that was in front of the house. I don't know whether he jumped over the wall, but they started shooting. I then turned around, threw myself forward. I was wounded then. Jakov fell over me. They continued shooting. I tried to hide myself. And then there was silence. After a while, after a short while, I heard some footsteps, and they disappeared. There was silence. I stood up, and then I fled to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take this part bit by bit. When you arrived, you arrived in the vicinity of a wall in front of a house. Did -- were you and the other persons in your group positioned in any way in particular near that wall?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They told us where we were to go. When this person appeared, when he reached the wall, well, that stone wall continued. It descended. This person wanted to take advantage of the opportunity to flee, and he jumped across -- over the wall. They shot after him -- they shot at him. And then Stipo Volic went to the other side. They started shooting at him and at us, and that's when I threw myself to the ground and tried to hide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said one person ran to one side over a wall and then Stipo Volic went to the other side and they started to shoot at them and to shoot at us." Now, I'd like you to explain to the Court what you mean by "they started to shoot at us." Apart from Stipo and the first person who ran, what were the rest of you doing when you say "they started to shoot at us"?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: They took us up to that point, and the first person reached the wall and they told us to stop. The first person jumped over the wall, the one who was right up next to the wall. He jumped over the wall. And they started shooting at him. And then this little one, he jumped to the other side. And then they all -- they started shooting at all of us. And when I saw that they had started shooting at us all, I threw myself to the ground, and that's when I was wounded. The others started falling to the ground too. Jakov fell over me and he died; he was killed. I tried to hide myself. They continued shooting. And then there was silence. They probably ran after this person who had fled. Someone had fled from that column. They disappeared at that time, and later I found out that two persons had fled. And when it became silent -- I didn't see that anyone was fleeing. And at that point I fled to the woods too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take this step by step. Just for clarification, when they started to shoot at what you say "us," what were you and that group doing? Were you running? Were you standing? Were you walking or what?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: As soon as I saw that they were shooting, I turned around and I threw myself down on my face, and I remained lying on the ground. And when it fell silent, these two persons fled. I stood up, and I could see that these people were on the ground. I then fled towards the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, about how many of you were there when they started to shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: There were 30 or 40 of us. We were all up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they started to shoot at you, at the time they started, what were you doing? Were you sitting, standing, walking, or running?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: We were all standing, apart from these two persons, Ante and the other one. They were in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many persons fired at you and the others as you stood there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: There were about ten of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you hit or were you not hit?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I was hit in the chest and the leg, but the wounds were superficial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you fell and someone fell on top of you. Do you know who fell on top of you, the name of the person who fell on top of you?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Jako Tavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, about how long did this shooting into the group of you who were standing there last for? How long -- or what period of time this lasted for? And you can give us an estimate.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Well, it was a few seconds. I don't know. Maybe ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I don't know, two, three, or five minutes. I don't know how long exactly. Because in such situations, it's difficult to know. When I heard these people fleeing, I stood up. I saw that there were people who had been killed and who were lying on the ground, and that's when I fled to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the firing -- well, did the firing stop while you were on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: The shooting stopped, and we remained silent. And when I heard that these two men were fleeing, I stood up and I fled. I didn't hear any other sounds. I stood up. I saw that there was no one there with weapons, and that's when I stood up and fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you stood up, can you just tell us what did you see, if anything, in your immediate vicinity of where you were and where the other men that were with you were.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I saw the dead people. I saw at the back of the column a man raised his head. He couldn't stand up. He must have been wounded in the lower part of the body, and he was crying out I don't know what. I didn't dare go there. I fled to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you eventually go to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I spent that day in the woods. 500 or 700 metres -- or 800 metres from the village. I spent the entire day there. I didn't dare go anywhere else, because I knew where their lines were. They were all around the place. I was near a pool. I drank some water, and a few hundred metres away from me there were BH army soldiers, and I heard someone crying out to someone else to bring him water. And then I carried on through the woods, and I remained there almost until dawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you end up or escape to eventually?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I later went through the woods to a village, Suhi Dol, and then over Brloge to Kosarici, where we used to have lines. And I saw further down there were two lines. And when I got to the place called Brloge, I heard shooting, and I waited. I stopped there, waited, waited until night fell. Then I descended, went below Suhi Dol. I saw Luka. I had a drink of water. And I went up towards the village of Orliste, and then through the place called Igrisce, which is where the Serbs held their lines. I had a sort of summer house there. And I lied down there until dawn. At daybreak, I saw troops over there, Serbian troops. I took my vest, tore it, raised it, and headed in their direction and cried out to them. When I reached, then they took me to the command, interrogated me there. Volic Stipan was there too. They questioned us, and then they took us down below to -- and around Babanovac, I was beaten. There were civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. So you surrendered to the Serb forces and eventually you were exchanged and returned to the fold of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you remember the names of some of the persons that you were with, that you were standing with at Bikose when they opened fire on you? And if you can remember the names, could you tell us slowly.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I remember Antara, they called him. That's the first person. And then Jako Tavic; he was with me. Pranjes Ana was in front of me. Jako Tavic. Ana Pranjes. Slavko Kramar. They were with me, and the person behind me, I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These names that you just called, have you seen any of them alive since that incident where you were shot at?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, Your Honours, that I am just about complete. But I was wondering if, with your permission, I could use the opportunity of an earlier adjournment to confer with my colleagues, if it is not inconvenient to the Court. I probably will end as soon as we resume, but I could use the time to speak with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is not a problem. But with regard to the witness, there are two questions I would like to ask the witness, because the Judges have to establish what the pertinence and the probative weight of his testimony is. I would like to know when he was escorted just before the shooting broke out, because one of his companions jumped over the wall, was the witness dressed in civilian or in military clothes. How was the witness dressed? The witness has told us that he tore up his vest when he surrendered to the Serbs. How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had a military jacket. All my clothes were military clothes. But the person who fled first, he was wearing a leather jacket, not a uniform, not a military uniform. He's the first person who jumped over the wall. But I had a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second question, which is very simple: You said that there were between 30 and 40 of you. The people who escorted you, how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who escorted us, the Mujahedin, there were -- and those with masks, there were about ten of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say "masks" - that's how it's been interpreted - do you mean a ski mask or a mask? Is mask is something one puts in front of us, and a ski mask is something one wears when it is cold. Would it be a mask or a ski mask? Since we're talking about the month of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had knitted caps on their head -- on their heads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's twenty to 4.00. We'll have what we call a technical break, which, according to the Rules, should be a 25-minute break. We will resume at five past 4.00, and the Prosecution will inform us of whether they're going to continue with their examination-in-chief or whether -- it will be time for the cross-examination. So the hearing is adjourned and we will resume at five past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. After the break, let's proceed with the hearing. Before we had our adjournment, the Prosecution said that they would let us know whether they wished to continue the examination-in-chief or whether they have concluded. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, if that may please you, that is the examination-in-chief. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm now going to give the floor to the Defence for the cross-examination, in conformity with Article 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Pranjes. My name is Edina Residovic, and I'm the Defence counsel for General Enver Hadzihasanovic. I shall be asking you a few questions about the same topics you discussed with my learned colleague of the Prosecution. Before your testimony here today, on several occasions you gave statements, the latest one being to the investigators of the OTP of The Hague Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And every time you did your best to tell them everything you remember, based on your personal knowledge; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you said that you lived in Maljine in the Travnik municipality; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to primary school in Guca Gora, which is about 2 and a half kilometres away from Maljine, and you went to secondary school in Travnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you confirmed here in court that as of the spring of 1990, until September 1992, you worked in Switzerland and would go back home to Travnik and Maljine from time to time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From October 1992, you were a member of the Croatian Defence Council or the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That autumn, when you returned to Maljine -- or rather, the Travnik municipality, you noticed in your area a certain number of foreigners, Mujahedins; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had taken up residence in empty houses in Poljanice near Mehurici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of that house, the Mujahedin kept watch throughout the day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know that a number of local Muslim inhabitants went to see and visit the Mujahedin and started copying them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Mujahedins were very different from the local population, both Muslim and Croatian; they had darker skin. They spoke a foreign language. They wore beards. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to your own position, as you described it to the Prosecutor, as a member of the Croatian Defence Council. Your particular unit at the time, at the beginning, belonged to the Travnik Brigade. And when the Frankopan Brigade was established, then you came under the Frankopan Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Frankopan Brigade had its headquarters at Guca Gora, not far from Maljine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to the north, above your villages, on Mount Vlasic that's where the front lines were facing the Serb army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until March 1993, your military assignment and that of the other HVO soldiers was to hold the line facing the Serb forces at Mount Vlasic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to you -- or rather, at the same positions on Mount Vlasic, the lines were also held by the BH army members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, but always above us, further up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the assignment you were given was to hold the line, and you did that by being up at the line, front line, for seven days and then you'd spend the following week resting at home; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers from Donje Maljine, when they went to take up their positions at the front line, facing the Serbs, had to pass by your village or through your village, the village of Gornje Maljine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993, armed conflicts took place in the broader area between the army and HVO in Busovaca, Kiseljak, and the surrounding parts; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that led to increased tension in your own village and increased fear as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your unit, in the early spring of 1993, for those reasons left its positions facing the Serb forces at Mount Vlasic and what you did was to start to defend your village and deploy there.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Guca Gora was where the HVO had its headquarters to control all passage to and from Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, perhaps you and I understand each other, but it would be a good idea to make it clearer to the other participants in the courtroom. Is it true that from Travnik to Zenica the main road passes through the Lasva River Valley, through Vitez and Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other road you can take from Travnik to Zenica leads across Guca Gora and Ovnak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: And there is another road leading through Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which leads on to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So one of the possible roads that you can take to go from Travnik to Zenica is the one passing through Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, and across Bila. You don't have to take the tubular road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. However, since you said a moment ago that at the beginning of 1993 a conflict broke out between the army and the HVO, is it correct that that main road, going through Vitez and Busovaca, was no longer open to the members of the BH army; they couldn't pass by that way?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't know, because I didn't take that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if there's anything you don't know, just say so. You can't answer something you don't know about. But let me go back to the day at which the events took place -- or rather, what you were saying. When you went back to Donje Maljine, your unit --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Gornje Maljine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Gornje Maljine. Your unit set up defence positions on the hill of Lazine.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: First of all they shot at us in Donje Polinje [phoen] and intercepted the road leading into our own village, Maljine. And then we established those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was up on Lazine hill above the village.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you this next question because I'm not quite sure whether you know anything about it, but here it is: Do you know that in the beginning of June in Travnik a conflict broke out between the BH army and the HVO? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: [Inaudible response].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't. Very well. You said that on the 7th of June, 1993, you were at your position between Maljine and Bikose at a place called Greda; is that right? You were on duty there.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And together with you there were Jako Tavic, Marijan Pavlic and Franjo Martinovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning of the 8th of June, you came under fire and you decided to withdraw towards the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this morning, when asked by the Prosecutor, you said that you took refuge in an improvised medical centre in the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the HVO members, all of you who had withdrawn to that place were under arms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. We did have weapons; that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that now in that medical centre there were a few wounded persons, members of the HVO, and some civilians; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you what happened exactly, but you said that at one particular point the members of the army asked you to surrender your weapons, the weapons you had with you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Puselja and a nurse negotiated with the members of the army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO soldiers who were there surrendered their weapons, but you did not surrender yours.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: No. I hid my weapon in the corn field, in a corner of the corn field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the wounded in the outpatients clinic was Ana Puselja; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken out of the clinic, you said that one of the soldiers asked you to drive a Lada vehicle in to him, which you did.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes. He was down by the garage, and he gave me the keys, car keys, and told me to drive the car out of the garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And this pregnant woman was put into that vehicle and driven off to Mehurici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: I don't know about that, because I left. So I don't know whether the -- that woman was driven off in that particular car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached the centre of the village, as you explained to the Prosecutor, the wounded persons who were in the clinic had already been driven off; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Now, they stayed there. Whether they were driven off later, I don't know. I can't say. All I know is that a wounded woman - and they had bandaged up her leg - was brought in there. The soldiers went to collect her and bring her into the clinic. And that's what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when you yourself left the village, the wounded persons and the doctor stayed on in the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact you don't actually know who took those wounded persons out of the village because you yourself had already left; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from your village towards Mehurici, you said you marched in a column of some sort and that you were escorted by several members of the BH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, and other civilians would join us on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But it was these army members, these soldiers, who tried to protect you, both from the civilians and from some insults that were being hurled at you; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point in time, you came across two Mujahedin who wanted to take a Croat out of the column; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of the army who were escorting you prevented that and didn't allow the man to be taken out, the HVO soldier to be separated from the column. They put him back into the column. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the road throughout, the soldiers' conduct towards you was quite proper; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one soldier even cautioned you and told you to take off a cross that you had on your shoulder because he said this could be dangerous if the Mujahedin were to see it, were to come and see it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heeded his advice and got rid of it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also explained to us, when asked by the Prosecutor, that at one point a group of armed Mujahedin turned up in front of the column and that they cocked their rifles at you straight away; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers of the BH army tried to explain that they were taking you to their headquarters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Mujahedin said that they wouldn't interfere because otherwise you might be killed.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, the Mujahedin had masks on, and they said that they would separate the men they wanted to take out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's when the separation started, after that; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Mujahedin, as you've already told us, separated 30 to 40 men, you amongst them, and the nurse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was in the hamlet of Bikose, this group of Mujahedin, joined by other Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, and they were masked too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, masked too. And I think you described what happened next in detail.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Among the 30 or 40, there were more people in civilian clothing than in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you've told the Court that too.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Most --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Most of them were in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Two were young boys who were not military-able men and one of them was a minor too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for answering my questions, and you have my sympathies for everything you had to go through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Now for the Kubura Defence. Any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No, there are no questions for Mr. Kubura for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Any redirect from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just one question of clarification, if it pleases you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when the Mujahedin who separated you came up, they said - and I'm going to read my note, which might be erroneous - but I have here that you said that the Mujahedin said "they wouldn't interfere because otherwise they might be killed." And you agreed with that. Could you explain to us what you meant when you agreed with that question or that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please give me the line on the transcript, because that's not the question I asked and that's not the answer the witness gave. So perhaps the interpretation was incorrect. Could you please give me the line on the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. On the English transcript, that's page 40, line 8. The question begins:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The Mujahedin said that they wouldn't interfere because otherwise you might be killed." Answer:

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: "Yes." And it goes on. My quotation of the question was not verbatim, was not exactly as it is, but the -- the basic aura of meaning was the same. Perhaps I could rephrase it based on what I see here. I have the verbatim transcript in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in answer to the statement, could the Mujahedin --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but perhaps there's been a mistake in the interpretation, but I can repeat the question to the witness, because what it says in the transcript, as interpreted by my colleague, was not part of either the question or the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, the Defence tells us that they never asked the witness that question. And the -- would the Prosecution like to continue with the question or to retract it? The Defence said they didn't ask the question that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The interpretation of my question was different to what I actually asked, and the answer that the witness gave is also different in view of the question we asked. So because of those reasons, I would like to draw your attention to that part of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the best way is to have Edina Residovic ask the question again and the witness can answer. So Ms. Ms. Residovic, could you ask your question again. Further cross-examination by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have understood what has happened. One of the questions I asked you was misinterpreted and what I asked you was this. At the moment when the group of Mujahedin jumped across the fence or hedge, the soldiers of the BH army attempted to intervene and they said that they would take you to the headquarters at Mehurici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the Mujahedin said to those soldiers, the soldiers of the BH army, not to interfere; otherwise, they'd kill you all. Is that what happened? Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Now, whether they said they would kill us all, I didn't understand that. But they jumped up in front of the group and cocked their rifles and they began to withdraw. Now, I didn't quite understand them -- I couldn't understand the Mujahedin, but the main thing was that the rifles were cocked and turned towards them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean towards the soldiers of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes, because they were between us and the Mujahedin, the ones with the caps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was only then that the members of the army withdrew, whereas the Mujahedin tried to -- started to separate you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO PRANJES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We now have the question at page 43, beginning with line 1 and onwards. Based on the answer given by the witness, would the Prosecution like to ask any more questions of this witness, Mr. Stamp, or does the answer suffice?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No further questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there are no further questions. Fine. Witness, the Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague. You have answered questions put to you by the Prosecution and the Defence, and we should like to thank you once again and wish you bon voyage back home. I would now like to ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before adjourning, since we have no other witnesses for today, I should like to indicate to the parties, to Mr. Bourgon especially, the procedure we are to follow once a request, a motion has been made from one of the parties, by one of the parties. If it comes from the Defence, then the Prosecution has 14 days within which to respond, and that is Article 126 bis in the Rules of Evidence and Procedure. Now, if the motion comes from the Prosecution, you have -- you also have 14 days to respond. Now, let's look at another hypothesis: Motion response. The party filing the motion considers that it has to respond to the response made by the Prosecution. So what happened in cases of that kind? This hypothesis has been regulated by a ruling given on the 9th of November, 2001, by the Pre-Trial Judge and it indicates the following: In cases of a possible reply, a motion, three days is granted for the parties to ask the Trial Chamber's authorisation to respond. Or to simplify this matter, a motion requires a response within 14 days. And let's take it that the Defence would like to respond to the response given; you have three days to reply to the Trial Chamber, either orally or in writing - orally would be quicker - to ask our authorisation to respond. So that is the procedure to follow. We took note that during the holiday break there were certain motions which did not follow that procedure, so this procedure is in place now both for the Defence and the Prosecution, to avoid one motion following another, et cetera. So this mechanism will be put in place. As far as procedure is concerned, it is the simplest one: Motion and answer, and a response again would require additional authorisation within the space of three days. So you can consult the ruling of the 9th of November, 2001, which stipulates procedure in instances of that kind. Now, would either of the two parties like to say anything? Any additional matters to raise or not for today? The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we know that we made a response outside the time limit mentioned today, as prescribed by the decision of the 9th of November, 2001. However, Your Honours, we were facing a dilemma. This ruling was issued by the Pre-Trial Judge, and it wasn't clear from it whether the time limits were linked to the pre-trial period. As there were the Christmas and New Year holidays, we weren't able to consult the Trial Chamber, and for that reason we made the exception. It is quite clear to us now that the Trial Chamber will follow that same ruling, the ruling of the 9th of November, 2001, in resolving these matters, and we shall adhere to it strictly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. Would the Prosecution like to raise any matters? Mr. Withopf?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: On this issue, Mr. President, Your Honours, we have no observations to make; however, it's quite obvious, and it's our understanding, that the ruling of the 9th of November, 2001, applied to both the pre-trial stage of the proceedings and the trial stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Under those circumstances, I adjourn the meeting for today and we resume tomorrow at 2.15, as usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be resumed on Wednesday, the 14 day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.40 p.m.,
